fr:mainmatter.fr:p: I vaguely recall reading that the tradition of isolating the non-logical symbols (constants, functions, relations) of a first order logic for a language \mathcal {L}, and referring to suitable models as \mathcal {L}-structures, was popularized by Carnap, and maybe in particular by The Logical Syntax of Language.
I am unable to track down a source for this now. I'll have to check The Syntax sometime. I can say at least Meaning and Necessity does not make use of this terminology in the same way.
